title: Layered safety harness for hybrid canaries and A/B experiments
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Production rollouts increasingly mix short-lived A/B experiments with long-running canaries and shadow lanes. Our existing controllers either focus on stepwise canaries or on simple A/B splitters; they don't provide a layered safety model that composes route-level statistical gates, session affinity, and an automated rollback saga that can coordinate multi-route reverts. This PR adds a lightweight "layered safety harness" that sits in the rollout controller and enables hybrid deployments: a canary can run alongside multiple A/B cohorts and shadow traffic, with shared metric gates and a coordinated rollback procedure that supports partial and full revert semantics.

Design summary: single-string description below covers the design, implementation notes, testing, and rollout plan.

Design: The harness composes three orthogonal layers: 1) Observability gates — per-metric detectors (latency, error-rate, quality-regression via eval hooks) that support configurable statistical tests (Welch t-test and MWW for non-normal distributions) and SLO-weighted thresholds. 2) Routing/affinity layer — deterministic session affinity keys can pin users to the same variant across canary and A/B cohorts; affinity decays and sticky TTLs are configurable per-route to avoid long-term skew. 3) Rollback saga — a stateful coordinator that persists the rollback plan (affected routes, cohorts, fallback model ids) and executes an orchestrated revert across services with safe pauses and verification checkpoints.

Key behaviors implemented: unified metric aggregation across shadowed and mirrored traffic so that shadow runs feed the same detectors without impacting live split ratios; cohort-aware ramping allowing A/B buckets to be promoted into canaries if safety gates pass; fail-fast vs graceful-degrade rollback modes; quorum checks when rolling back multi-region configurations.

Checklist (implemented): - [x] Metric gate framework with pluggable statistical tests and lookback window config - [x] Session affinity plumbing and TTL semantics in router - [x] Saga-based rollback coordinator with idempotent steps and compensation actions - [x] YAML CRD for layered harness configuration with sane defaults and examples - [x] End-to-end e2e tests (local and CI harness) that simulate noisy traffic and injected regressions - [x] Docs: console UX additions and rollout runbook snippets

Backward compatibility: existing rollout manifests continue to work unchanged; harness is opt-in via a new field in the RolloutSpec (safety.harness: enabled). Default is disabled. No changes to client APIs.

Testing notes: Unit tests for gate math and tie-breaking semantics. Integration tests use a synthetic traffic generator that exercises A/B splits, sticky sessions, and shadow mirrors; recovered from injected 5xx spike and verified rollback saga correct ordering. CI includes an e2e suite flagged as slow; the PR marks those tests to run in the nightly matrix but includes a short fast path for standard PR runs.

Risk and mitigations: The primary risk is noisy statistical signals causing false positives; mitigated by conservative default thresholds, mandatory min-sample-size and bootstrapped confidence intervals. Rollback actions are executed in transactional steps with verification delays and the option to abort if verification fails repeatedly.

Related work: builds on ENG-3222 (rollout controller refactor) and ENG-4030 (session affinity router). See linked Linear tickets.

Rollout plan: canary branch deploy to staging for 48 hours, shadow experiments enabled for two internal apps, then gradual enable in canary clusters with feature flag. Monitor dashboard and alerting for regressions; on-call runbook referenced in docs.

review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): The gate math looks solid but I'm concerned about false positives from small cohorts. Can we enforce a min-sample-size at the API surface and make it non-optional for t-test gates?
Aisha Patel (author): Good catch — added a minSampleSize field with a conservative default (200 users) and validation in API -> implemented in commit bda7c6f.
Priya Desai (reviewer): Saga persistence needs compaction to avoid unbounded journal growth. Also, what happens if the coordinator loses leader elections mid-saga?

Aisha Patel (author): Saga journal has compaction on completion and a TTL for tombstones; the coordinator uses the existing leader election library with retries. Added explicit step-level idempotency checks and re-claim logic; details in saga/rollback_coordinator.go. See commit d3e8b7a.
Omar Haddad (reviewer): e2e test was flaky on first run due to race in affinity TTL expiry — suggest deterministic clocks in tests.
Aisha Patel (author): Updated tests to use a fake clock and tightened TTL handling; re-ran e2e in CI — stabilized.

release_notes:
- Introduce Layered Safety Harness (opt-in) for composing canaries, A/B cohorts, and shadowing with shared metric gates and saga rollback
- New CRD fields: safety.harness.enabled, safety.harness.minSampleSize, safety.harness.rollbackMode
- Session affinity TTLs and deterministic routing keys for stable A/B experience
- Console: rollout detail UI shows harness status and gate outcomes
merge_note: Squash-merged after addressing reviewers' feedback. CI green on final run. Deployed to staging stacks behind feature flag.
